facts.statement: Zoneait is an extinct genus of marine crocodile relative known only from the species Zoneait nargorum.
facts.quote: Zoneait (pronounced "zone-eight" and meaning "large tooth" in the Kiowa language) is an extinct genus of thalattosuchian crocodylomorph known from a single species, Zoneait nargorum, from the Middle Jurassic Snowshoe Formation of Oregon.

facts.statement: The species was named in 2015 by Eric Wilberg based on partial skulls, vertebrae, and forelimb bones found near Izee, Oregon.
facts.quote: Z. nargorum was named in 2015 by paleontologist Eric Wilberg on the basis of some partial skulls, vertebrae, and forelimb bones that were found in an outcrop of the Weberg Member of the Snowshoe Formation near the town of Izee.

facts.statement: Zoneait belongs to the clade Metriorhynchoidea, which included marine crocodile relatives that lived until the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: It is a member of Metriorhynchoidea, a clade of marine-adapted thalattosuchians that existed until the Early Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Zoneait possessed a streamlined skull with expanded prefrontals that supported eyes facing to the sides.
facts.quote: The skull of Zoneait has expanded prefrontals, which support laterally-facing eyes. In combination with a streamlined skull, which is notably more derived than other non-metriorhynchid members of Metriorhynchoidea.

facts.statement: Zoneait had forelimbs that were not flattened into paddles, but its lower arm bone (ulna) was reduced in length while the upper arm bone remained unchanged.
facts.quote: The forelimbs are not flattened into paddles as in metriorhynchids, but the ulna (lower arm bone) is reduced in length, indicating that forelimb reduction began at the lower limb and progressed upward (the humerus or upper arm bone of Zoneait not reduced).

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the adaptation of metriorhynchoids to marine life began with changes in feeding ecology before changes in swimming locomotion occurred.
facts.quote: Taken together, the transitional features of Zoneait indicate that metriorhynchoids' adaptation of a marine lifestyle began with a shift in feeding ecology and only later involved changes in swimming locomotion.

facts.statement: The skull of Zoneait shows evidence of salt glands with elongated passages for the carotid artery, which may have increased blood flow to the glands.
facts.quote: El cráneo de Zoneait además muestra evidencias de glándulas salinas con los pasajes alargados para la arteria carótida, los cuales pudieron haber incrementado el flujo sanguíneo a las glándulas.

facts.statement: Zoneait lived between 174.7 and 168.2 million years ago during the Aalenian to Bajocian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Aalenian to Bajocian (174.7 to 168.2 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Zoneait lived in a shallow marine environment within a tropical forearc basin and is considered a marine predator.
rejected.quote: The Snowshoe Formation was deposited in a shallow marine environment within a tropical forearc basin, suggesting that Zoneait was a marine predator.
